lesson.title: Food and everyday meals — Form and meaning
learning_goals: Establish a usable lexical representation and use it in a simple communicative exchange.
Find explicitly stated people, actions, objects and locations in short texts.
Recognise familiar words and retrieve a stated item, number or place without relying on the transcript.
Give an intelligible personal answer using two linked statements.
Write complete SVO sentences with clear reference and basic punctuation.

targets.label: Subject + present-tense verb + object with I/you/we/they
Object nouns; receptive recognition of eats/drinks with named subjects; capital I and final full stop
Find explicitly stated people, actions, objects and locations in short texts.
Recognise familiar words and retrieve a stated item, number or place without relying on the transcript.
Give an intelligible personal answer using two linked statements.
Write complete SVO sentences with clear reference and basic punctuation.
Word boundaries, stressed syllables, clear final consonants and meaningful pauses
Understand the four skill names; distinguish an answer from an explanation; type exact words. Do not impose full-test timing.
Identify a mismatch, correct it and retrieve the capability in a fresh context without overwriting the first attempt.

content_gaps: Natural listening recordings and pronunciation assets are not supplied.
Sealed transfer items, reference-anchored productive assessment and empirical item calibration are not supplied.
Dictionary/corpus checks and distractor review are still required.
Authoring placeholder fields are not production component configuration; compile only against verified runtime contracts.

design.sequence_strategy: Keep the mandated vocabulary intake and dictation first; teach the unit language, bridge print to speech, integrate both receptive skills, expand the primary lesson role, produce, revise and check fresh transfer. Optional target repairs are conditional specifications, not a fixed compulsory sequence.
notes: A linear order implements the authoring prerequisite graph; this does not assume a deployed runtime DAG engine.
All curriculum target selections and exact counts are Vocora design choices, not validated IELTS-band mappings.
Optional repair dispatch and readiness routing are proposed product behavior.
First-attempt evidence, repaired performance and official IELTS scoring must remain separate.

slides.purpose: Explain the unit grammar through a worked contrast.

data.prompt_or_stimulus:
MODEL: I eat rice.

TARGET: Subject + present-tense verb + object with I/you/we/they

slides.purpose: Read for the main message before selecting details.

data.instruction_intent: Read for the main message before selecting details.
data.prompt_or_stimulus:
AUTHORED REFERENCE EX01-R, a focused extract rather than a full-length stage assessment:
My name is Mina. I eat bread in the morning. I drink milk. My brother, Sam, eats rice at lunch. He drinks water. We eat at home. Our table is small. In the evening, I eat rice and Sam eats bread. We both drink water. We like our meals. On Sunday, our friend Jo eats with us at home.
data.expected_response: State a defensible gist; keep the coherent text accessible during practice.
data.feedback_intent: The first skim precedes questions; do not display an answer summary in a scored task.
